Divine guidance native text source and popup path

Source images come from data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. Addresses below are
RVAs, with reference first and classic second. Source extraction reads the PE
image and uses the fixed native objdump; it does not load or attach to the game.
The owner was located by the actual RIP operand for the greeting, and its end
includes the PE chained unwind ranges.

Producer owner: 7eed80..7f3ca2 / 7ec600..7f1522.
The complete annotated owners, text helper bodies, literal operands, direct
calls and conditional branches are retained in the adjacent source files.
divine-utterance-branches.tsv reconstructs 29 divine utterance alternatives per
edition, plus the default and RAW supplied curse description alternatives.
It preserves the original native double spaces and quote characters. Its
descriptive placeholders identify the actual field kind; these are source
annotations and are not runtime translation placeholder syntax.

Greeting construction at 7f04d1..7f0762 / 7edd51..7edfe2:

    text = '"Greetings.  I am ' + historical_figure(deity_id)
         + ', and I have chosen you'
    if deity.sphere_info != null and sphere_info.spheres != null
       and spheres.size() != 0:
        text += ' as my instrument of ' + sphere_name(spheres[0])
    text += '.  '
    for index, inorganic in world.raws.inorganics:
        if inorganic.flags.test(0x15):
            text += 'The remnants of creation, '
                 + material_name(type=0, index=index, flags=0,
                                 adjective=false, state=0)
                 + ', belong with my followers, '
                 + entity_name(guidance.followers_entity_id, flags=0)
                 + '.  '
            break
    text += 'Seek out ' + historical_figure(guidance.representative_id)
         + ' in ' + abstract_building_name(guidance.site_id,
                                          guidance.building_id,
                                          prefer_name=true, flags=0)
         + ' and fulfill your destiny."'

The optional sphere clause and remnant clause are independent: all four
combinations are reachable. The selected material is the first matching
inorganic, not an entity name. The final field is an abstract building within a
site, not the site name. The material, followers and building fields may each
contain spaces; whole native fields must remain intact when translating.
The complete text is submitted as announcement type 0x15f (351), color 7,
bright 1, timer 2000 and portrait historical-figure ID equal to the deity ID.

Further divine utterances in the same owner are: finding the representative;
leaving the current structure before travel; sensing the representative;
securing the treasure; finding the quest site; advising faster travel to that
site; danger at the destination entrance; approaching the entrance; fulfilling
the quest; following the return direction; gifting/dropping the treasure;
giving it to other worshippers; the apostate response; and ending travel near
the destination. Their exact complete source sentences are in
divine-utterance-branches.tsv, with producer RVAs and native literal evidence
in native-literals.tsv.

Approaching the entrance, 7f1c76..7f1df9 / 7ef4f6..7ef679:

    text = '"You are close.  Follow your senses to the entrance.'
    if controlled_unit != null:
        hunger = controlled_unit[0x988] >= 0xe100  (57600)
        thirst = controlled_unit[0x98c] >= 0xe100  (57600)
        sleep  = controlled_unit[0x990] >= 0x1c200 (115200)
        if hunger or thirst or sleep:
            text += '  But my chosen, you are '
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (1,1,1): text += 'in a state'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (1,1,0): text += 'in need of drink and sustenance'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (1,0,1): text += 'in need of sustenance and sleep'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (1,0,0): text += 'in need of sustenance'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (0,1,1): text += 'in need of drink and sleep'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (0,1,0): text += 'in need of drink'
            if (hunger,thirst,sleep) == (0,0,1): text += 'in need of sleep'
            text += '!  See to yourself before you face what\'s ahead.'
            if thirst:
                position = unit_position(controlled_unit)  // 1367430
                if position.x != -30000:
                    temperature = world_temperature(position)  // 247cf0
                    if unsigned_word(temperature) <= 10000:
                        text += '  Remember that ice and snow can be heated by a campfire.'
    text += '"'

There is a plain variant, seven need variants, and four additional ice/snow
variants for the thirst-containing states. The control flow and thresholds are
identical in both images; these are twelve complete alternatives.

After the apostate response, curse execution creates one of two different
constructions:

    if interaction_source.trigger_string_second(+0x70).empty():
        text = 'You have been cursed by ' + deity_name + '!'
    else:
        text = 'You ' + interaction_source.trigger_string_second(+0x70)
                     + ' ' + interaction_source.trigger_string(+0xb0)

The RAW branch does not append ' by ', the deity name or a final exclamation
mark. Those may only occur if they are already present in the RAW strings.
Both versions compute the deity name before this condition, but only the
default branch appends it. Reference 7f27b3 / classic 7f0033 branches to the
default when trigger_string_second is empty. The RAW branch appends the two
RAW strings at 7f27b5..7f27e9 / 7f0035..7f0069, then jumps directly to the
announcement submission setup at 7f2835 / 7f00b5.

The field identities are defined by
data/upstream/df-structures/df.interaction.xml: interaction_source has name at
0x10, hist_string_1 at 0x30, hist_string_2 at 0x50,
trigger_string_second (IS_TRIGGER_STRING_SECOND) at 0x70,
trigger_string_third at 0x90, and trigger_string (IS_TRIGGER_STRING) at 0xb0.
The RAW suffix is the trigger text, not the history text and not a deity field.
The non-default construction uses RAW interaction text, not finite PE literals.
This same root owner also contains unrelated control/sleep announcements such
as tactical control, awakening and interrupted sleep. Those operands are
retained in the complete owner extraction rather than mislabelled divine
dialogue. Other announcement types can share the same native popup class; the
popup capture mechanism described below is not tied to the four greeting
templates.

Dynamic text providers

historical_figure: b92f10 / b8ff50. The greeting constructs a fresh reference
context through 72080 / 72010: flags 0, perspective pointers null, subject and
speaker IDs -1. Both word parameters are 0,1. Valid named figures use the full
English language name at historical_figure+0x38 via a946e0 / a91760, with English
true and first-name-only false. An absent ID yields 'an unknown creature'. A
valid nameless figure yields 'a ' plus optional 'zombie ' and/or 'ghostly ',
the RAW creature/caste name, and optional generated creature text from the
figure's generated-info object. The caste provider is aa3bd0 / aa0c50; its body
is also extracted. The helper has additional interrogation, perspective,
pronoun, possession and LPAGE branches, but this default context does not
select them. The second word parameter 1 suppresses the additional named-figure
caste descriptor path; a named divine field is its complete language name.

sphere: 756690 / 7540b0. The complete 130-entry branch table maps enum 0..129 to
bare sphere nouns. Out-of-range enum produces 'no sphere'. Every enum and actual
literal operand is retained in finite-field-values.tsv. The native producer
uses the first sphere only, so joins of multiple spheres cannot arise here.

material: 14d1920 / 14cc890; lookup 14add70 / 14a8ce0. The actual call has material
type 0, the selected inorganic vector index, flags 0, adjective false, state 0
(SOLID). Lookup reads the world inorganics at world+0x11b3d8..0x11b3e0 and returns
inorganic+0x1a8. The formatter appends the nonempty material prefix string at
material+0x520 and one space, then the state-name string at material+0xb8 for
SOLID. Thus the native source is the RAW material's state name (possibly with
its native prefix). Null material yields 'unknown material'. Other formatter
branches for cloth, wood, figure-derived materials etc are retained in the
callee extraction, but are unreachable with the greeting's type-0 arguments.

followers entity: b92900 / b8f940. Named entities use their full English language
name at entity+0x20. Missing entity yields 'an unknown civilization'. Flags 0
means no LPAGE wrapping.

quest site in later advice: b93930 / b90970. Uses the full native site name and
falls back to 'an unknown site'. These two later advice fields are sites; they
are distinct from the greeting's abstract-building field.

abstract building: b94090 / b910d0. The producer passes site ID and abstract
building ID, prefer_name=true, flags=0. A valid building with a nonnull virtual
getName() (vtable+0x10), whose language_name+0x72 has_name byte is true, uses its
full English language name. Otherwise its native virtual type selects the
following complete field values:

    0 a mead hall; 1 a keep; 2 a temple; 3 a dark tower; 4 a market;
    5 a tomb; 6 subtype 0 a dungeon, 1 the sewers, 2 the catacombs;
    7 an underworld spire; 8 a tavern; 9 a library; 10 a counting house;
    11 a guildhall; 12 a tower; 13 a hospital.

Invalid type or missing site/building yields 'an unknown building'. A valid
type-6 building with an invalid subtype appends no field text. All enum
destinations and literal operands are retained in finite-field-values.tsv.
The formatter's LPAGE branches are unreachable with the producer's flags 0.

Procedurally generated names and RAW field strings are not a finite sentence
catalog. Their complete native suppliers and the argument restrictions are
the translation boundary; treating their words as unrelated literals loses
the name or material grammar.

Native popup creation, storage, layout and drawing

Manager: reference global RVA 24e3850 / classic global RVA 24dd740.
Manager fields have the same offsets in both images:

    +0x30,+0x38,+0x40  popup vector begin,end,capacity (popup pointers)
    +0x48,+0x50,+0x58  markup word vector begin,end,capacity (word pointers)
    +0x60,+0x68,+0x70  markup link vector begin,end,capacity
    +0x78             markup width
    +0x7c             final native row index (layout maximum y)
    +0x80             markup environment
    +0x88             portrait historical-figure ID

Each popup is allocated by e3880 / e3810 with size 0x28:

    +0x00  MSVC std::string full original text, size+0x10, capacity+0x18
    +0x20  color short
    +0x22  bright byte
    +0x24  portrait historical-figure ID int

Announcement submission e3c20 / e3bb0 queues this popup at e4330 / e42c0, copies
the complete original string at e4352 / e42e2, and stores the color/bright and
portrait metadata. For the active first popup, it resets markup through
e37d0 / e3760, appends the original text at e43d9 / e4369 through
d51eb0 / d4eef0, and lays it out at e43ea / e437a through d51c80 / d4ecc0 using
native width 50. The portrait ID is stored at e43f9 / e4389.

Each markup word has size 0x38:

    +0x00  MSVC std::string word or punctuation/control source
    +0x20  red byte; +0x21 green byte; +0x22 blue byte
    +0x24  link index
    +0x28  native column int
    +0x2c  native row int
    +0x30  control flags

Ordinary word storage comes from d544e0 / d51520. Control words are initialized
with x=-1,y=-1 and empty source. The native wrap loop d51c80 / d4ecc0 skips the
ordinary coordinate assignment for flags &1, &2 and &4, instead changing the
current line/paragraph state. It places normal text and punctuation using the
native word lengths and row/column positions. These coordinates describe the
displayed paragraph even when native drawing splits one sentence into many
calls.

The actual popup renderer is e9f40..ea4c8 / e9ed0..ea458. It receives the manager
pointer in RCX. It reads word vector manager+0x48..0x50 at ea0f9 / ea089; for each
word it sets native RGB and screen cursor, then calls ad9960 / ad69a0 at
ea17c / ea10c using the original word object as the std::string source. Native
screen positions are:

    left = midpoint(incoming min_x, incoming max_x) - 26
    right = left + 53
    height = markup.max_y + 8
    top = midpoint(init.display.grid_y) - midpoint(height)
    if graphics portrait enabled and portrait ID != -1:
        height = max(height,10)
        left -= 6
        right += 6
        text_x = left + 14 + word.x
    else:
        text_x = left + 2 + word.x
    text_y = top + 2 + word.y
    button_top = top + height - 4
    body_bottom_exclusive = button_top

init.display.grid_y is the init global at reference RVA 0x23cd788 and classic
RVA 0x23c7678. It precedes world (reference 0x23d14f0), so the world-schema
resolver native_history_global cannot resolve it and returns zero. Read it
through the reviewed PE edition binding. The popup queue and markup remain
world.status schema fields, unlike this independent display setting.

The renderer does not read word control flags; it calls the string drawer for
every pointer in the word vector. The drawer ad9960 / ad69a0 immediately returns
for std::string size==0 (reference ad997d..ad9982), so empty control words draw
nothing. Capturing visible source words should omit empty strings and invalid
negative native coordinates. It must not require every control word to yield
rendered cells. Valid text words retain native object addresses and coordinates
for aligning the translated full paragraph with its original draw calls.

This is ordinary full-row text, not a TOP_OF_TEXT/BOTTOM_OF_TEXT caption.
The reference drawer calls bb190 at ad9a00. That character writer updates the
glyph/RGB and clears the primary texture at bb31c..bb323, but does not update
the half-font flag array. Covered page flags therefore cannot identify this
popup's words as two halves or replace its paragraph-wide clearing geometry.

The More and Okay labels are inline immediate native strings at reference
ea42e / ea457, classic ea3be / ea3e7. More appears when the popup queue has more
than one item. Input owner 8b91c0 / 8b6a40 removes the current first popup and,
if another remains, resets/appends/wraps the new front text through the same
markup helpers. Popup save owner 7aa300 / 7a7d20 is serialization, not rendering.

Direct callers of the actual popup renderer are retained in
popup-render-callers.tsv and the two popup-render-callers.asm files:

    reference 3fb4ed (owner 3d6950), 7f3e2e (owner 7f3cb0),
              810d0a (owner 80d5e0)
    classic   3f90ad (owner 3d4510), 7f16ae (owner 7f1530),
              80e58a (owner 80ae60)

The adventure renderer call is immediately after 7f3e0c -> af1190. The caller
then obtains x bounds via c33370 and calls the popup renderer directly. Thus
af1190 itself need not read the popup word globals for this popup to appear.

The generic paragraph producer 8e7310 is not on this source path. Merely
changing a sentence catalog or relying on that paragraph capture leaves the
active popup's split native word calls uncovered. Existing history markup
hooks use the same d51eb0/d51c80/ad9960 helpers at different callsites; they do
not establish ownership for e43d9/e43ea/ea17c. The reliable native boundary here
is the active manager queue's full source string together with its word vector
and coordinates, or hooks explicitly scoped to these popup callsites.
